title: Dairy-Free Mint Chocolate Cupcakes
shortDescription: Rich cocoa cupcakes with a swirl of dairy-free mint frosting, ready in about 45 minutes total.
description: These cupcakes pair a deep cocoa cake with a cool mint frosting swirl. I tested this batch in my own kitchen using coconut oil and almond milk, and the crumb stayed soft and moist without a drop of dairy. The mint frosting uses dairy-free butter and a touch of peppermint extract, so it tastes bright, not toothpasty. Swirl it high for that classic bakery look. This is a great pick if you want a chocolate mint treat that fits a dairy-free kitchen. It also works well for parties since the finish is refreshing, not heavy. I like to add a few chocolate shavings on top for contrast. The dark cocoa and pale green frosting look great together on a plate.
ingredients: 1/3 cup melted coconut oil, cooled slightly
1 to 2 tbsp almond milk, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix sugar, coconut oil, almond milk, vinegar, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix. Stir just until combined, no lumps of flour.
Divide batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes.
Move cupcakes to a wire rack and let them cool fully before frosting.
Beat dairy-free butter until fluffy, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in peppermint extract and almond milk until the frosting is smooth and pipeable. Add green coloring if using.
Pipe a tall swirl on each cupcake and top with chocolate shavings.
tips: Chill the frosting for 10 minutes if it feels too soft to pipe a tall swirl.
Use natural cocoa powder for a slightly tangier chocolate taste, or dutch process for a smoother, darker crumb.
Start with 1/4 teaspoon peppermint extract and taste before adding more. It gets strong fast.
Store cupcakes in the fridge and let them sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before serving.

faq.question: Can I use mint extract instead of peppermint extract?
faq.answer: Yes, but mint extract is milder. Use double the amount and taste the frosting before piping.

faq.question: Will coconut oil make the cupcakes taste like coconut?
faq.answer: No, refined coconut oil has almost no flavor. It just adds moisture without any dairy.

faq.question: How do I keep the frosting from turning too dark green?
faq.answer: Add food coloring one drop at a time. A pale mint shade looks more natural against the dark cake.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead for a party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes a day ahead and store them covered at room temperature. Frost them the morning of your event.

conclusion: These cupcakes give you that cool mint and chocolate combo without any dairy. The cake stays moist, and the frosting swirl makes them look bakery ready.
